title: Finite smooth trace and coefficient reduction over an arbitrary ground field
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $k$ be any field of characteristic different from $\ell$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], smooth of pure relative dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For $n\geq1$ set $A_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and for $T=X,Y$ write $A_{n,T}$ for its constant sheaf on $T$. On each small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)$ consist of complexes with bounded constructible cohomology in the intrinsic finite-stratification sense of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and finite Tor amplitude: there are integers $a\leq b$ such that tensoring with any sheaf of $A_n$-modules in degree zero has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Let $Rf_{!,n}$ be compact-support direct image, formed by proper direct image after extension by zero in a compactification [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and define its constructible exceptional inverse image as follows. Write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site comparison and $f_n^\times$ for the right adjoint of ordinary etale compact-support direct image. For $K$ of bounded constructible etale origin $K_0$, put $Rf_n^!K=\nu_X^*f_n^\times K_0$, using the fully faithful comparison to identify different choices of $K_0$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin, thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Preservation of bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude for this smooth $f$ is part of the assertion below. Write $A_{n,T}(1)=\mu_{\ell^n,T}$, the sheaf of $\ell^n$-th roots of unity, $A_{n,T}(d)=\mu_{\ell^n,T}^{\otimes_{A_n}d}$ with zeroth power $A_{n,T}$, and $K(d)=K\otimes^L_{A_n} A_{n,T}(d)$ [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf, def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

The SGA-normalized smooth trace $Rf_{!,n}(Lf^*K(d)[2d])\to K$ [lem-pur-torsion-top-trace] has adjoint an isomorphism
$$\gamma_{n,K}:Lf^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_n^!K$$
for every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_n)$. Here the normalization is the trace of SGA 4 XVIII 2.9, 2.13.2 and 3.2.5; at relative dimension zero it is the etale adjunction. For every $n\geq1$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{n+1})$, the comparisons are compatible with the quotient map $A_{n+1}\to A_n$: derived reduction of $\gamma_{n+1,K}$ is $\gamma_{n,K\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n}$ under the pullback, twist and exceptional-image coefficient comparisons. Reduction from $A_r$ to $A_n$ agrees with successive reduction through $A_m$ for all $r\geq m\geq n\geq1$ under tensor associativity (the quotient cocycle).

For $K=A_{n,Y}$ the source and target of $\gamma_{n,K}$ have constructible cohomology only in degree $-2d$; their reductions, identified by these comparisons, satisfy the quotient cocycle.

source.place: XVIII Theorem 3.2.5, pp. 585–586; trace 2.9, 2.13.2; coefficient induction 3.1.12 and 3.1.12.1. Compatibility with derived coefficient reduction and its quotient cocycle is the additional comparison assertion for these normalized trace constructions; 3.1.12.1 itself states restriction-of-scalars compatibility.

proof.text: Ordinary-etale setting and the trace map. A field is Noetherian (its ideals are $0$ and the whole field), so $X,Y$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The graph of $f$ is closed in $X\times_kY$ because $Y$ is separated over $k$; the projection $X\times_kY\to Y$ is separated finite type, being the base change of the separated finite-type map $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Factoring $f$ as its closed graph followed by this projection proves that $f$ is separated finite type; [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies a compactification. For a finite coefficient ring $A=A_n$, write $P_A=Rf^{\mathrm{et}}_{!,A}$ and $G_A=f_A^\times$. Their ordinary-etale adjunction exists by [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] makes the compact-support functor and its composition comparisons independent of this choice. Set $H_AK=f^*K(d)[2d]$. The twists and their independence of the annihilating power of $\ell$ are those of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The new top-degree trace theorem [lem-pur-torsion-top-trace] applies: a smooth $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]; it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated since it is separated finite type, hence of finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. It has pure relative dimension $d$, and $\ell$ is invertible. Let $T^A_K:P_AH_AK\to K$ be its specified trace, and let $\gamma^A_K:H_AK\to G_AK$ be its adjoint. This constructs the map without assuming it invertible.

source.place: 2.9, 2.13.2 and 3.2.3; ordinary adjunction as in 3.1, and Noetherian compactification prerequisites.

proof.text: Nondegeneracy is local on the source and reduces to affine space. By [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form], $X$ has an open cover by affine $u:U\hookrightarrow X$ on which $f u$ factors as $U\xrightarrow{e}\mathbf A^d_V\xrightarrow{p}V\xrightarrow{v}Y$, with $V$ affine, $v$ open and $e$ etale. The rank is $d$ since $f$ has pure relative dimension $d$. The schemes $U,V,\mathbf A^d_V$ are Noetherian. The maps $u,v$ are quasi-compact open immersions, hence separated finite type; $p$ is affine of finite type; and $e$ is a morphism of affine schemes, hence separated and quasi-compact, and is locally of finite presentation because it is etale. Thus $e$ is also finite type. Their composites are separated finite type, and [thm-nagata-compactification] applies to these Noetherian, hence quasi-compact quasi-separated, targets. The exact sum adjunction and its compact-support normalization are [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] and [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization]. Composing these adjunctions using [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] identifies $u^*G_AK$ with $e^*p_A^\times v^*K$. The trace transitivity and etale normalization in [lem-pur-torsion-top-trace] identify the adjoint of the trace for $fu$ with the composite of $e^*\gamma^A_{p,v^*K}$ and these adjunction identifications: explicitly the corresponding counit is first the etale sum counit $e_!e^*\to1$, then $T^A_{p,v^*K}$, then the open sum counit $v_!v^*\to1$. It is also $u^*\gamma^A_{f,K}$ under source locality, by the same trace restriction formula and the adjunction bijection. The affine-space unit trace in the new theorem equals [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]; hence [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity], specialized to $F=\mathbf Q_\ell$, $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ and the trivial rank-$d$ bundle over $V$, proves $\gamma^A_{p,v^*K}$ invertible. Therefore every $u^*\gamma^A_{f,K}$ is invertible. The cohomology sheaves of its cone restrict to zero on the open cover, so they are zero, proving $\gamma^A_{f,K}$ invertible. This reasoning concerns actual counits and their adjoints, and does not test equality of derived morphisms on geometric stalks.

source.place: 2.9 Var.3, 2.10, 3.2.3–3.2.5; etale-local affine-space argument using the existing normalized vector-bundle adjunction.

proof.text: Transfer to the intrinsic categories, including the Tor bound. Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$. Every intrinsic $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ has bounded constructible etale origin $K_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. The comparison is exact [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], fully faithful on $D^+$ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], and preserves derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. If $K$ has Tor interval $[a,b]$, then for every ordinary module sheaf $M$, $C_Y(K_0\otimes_A^LM)=K\otimes_A^LC_YM$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$. Exactness and full faithfulness on sheaves imply that $C_Y$ detects a zero cohomology sheaf, so $K_0$ has the same Tor interval. Choose its bounded flat model in $[a,b]$ by [lem-sf-etale-flat-model]; it is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Pullback preserves K-flatness and flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and twists are flat rank-one sheaves by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Thus $H_AK_0$ and $C_XH_AK_0$ have Tor interval $[a-2d,b-2d]$. Their cohomology is constructible: exact inverse image pulls a finite locally closed stratification back to one on $X$, on each stratum preserving finite locally constant sheaves, and tensoring a locally free line preserves them. Use [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] for $C_Xf^*=f^*C_Y$. The compact-support comparison is the composite of the open comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] and the proper comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. The latter is expressly the adjoint-of-counit map, so the composed comparisons identify the transported adjunction and its counit, not merely the two objects. In particular the ordinary trace above maps to the SGA-normalized pro-etale trace. By the displayed definition of the transported functor, $Rf_n^!K=C_XG_AK_0$, and its trace-adjoint map is $C_X\gamma^A_{K_0}$ under the displayed comparisons. Step 2 proves the asserted isomorphism, and the source computation just made supplies the required bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude of the target. No right adjoint on the entire pro-etale derived category is invoked.

source.place: 3.2.5, with the ordinary-etale adjunction transported through the explicitly cited site comparisons; flat models supply the constructible finite-Tor restriction.

proof.text: Derived reductions and their pullback/twist identifications. Let $r\geq m\geq1$, $A=A_r$, $B=A_m$, and $S_T(-)=(-)\otimes_A^LB$. Use the everywhere-defined K-flat construction in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For finite-Tor $K$, a bounded flat model $Q$ exists as in Step 3; $Q\otimes_AB$ is a bounded flat $B$-model. Indeed tensoring its terms with an exact sequence of $B$-modules is the same as tensoring $Q$ with the underlying exact sequence of $A$-modules. It is K-flat since for any acyclic $B$-complex $L$, $(Q\otimes_AB)\otimes_BL=Q\otimes_A\operatorname{Res}L$ is acyclic. It has the same degree interval, so $SK$ remains bounded and finite Tor. Its cohomology is intrinsically constructible by [lem-pur-finite-tensor-constructible-cohomology], applied with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, level $r$, and $L$ the constant finite sheaf $B$. This is also constructibility as a $B$-module sheaf: on every stratum a local constant $A$-module presentation is automatically $B$-linear, because the surjection $A\to B$ makes the $B$-action uniquely determined by the $A$-action, and its finite stalks remain finite over $B$. Hence it again has etale origin by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. The tensor/pullback comparison from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives $S_Xf_A^*K\cong f_B^*S_YK$. The power map $\mu_{\ell^r}\to\mu_{\ell^m}$ induces $\mu_{\ell^r}\otimes_AB\cong\mu_{\ell^m}$ by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]; in a local primitive-root generator it sends the generator to the generator. These flat lines require no higher derived tensor terms. Taking $d$ tensor powers and shifting gives a canonical $\lambda_K:S_XH_AK\cong H_BS_YK$. For $r\geq m\geq n$, all reassociations on the flat model are $(q\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto q\otimes bc$, and power maps multiply exponents. Consequently the reduction associativity and the $\lambda$ identifications satisfy the quotient cocycle, including $r=m$ and $d=0$.

source.place: 1.1.1 (independence of annihilator), 2.13.2; derived scalar extension and associativity computed on the cited flat models.

proof.text:
Construct the compact-support coefficient comparison, retaining $B$-linearity. For an ordinary bounded finite-Tor $A$-complex $M$, define
$$c_M:S_YP_AM\longrightarrow P_BS_XM$$
using a compactification $f=rj$. For the open part the map $(j_!Q)\otimes_AB\to j_!(Q\otimes_AB)$ is the identity $q\otimes b\mapsto q\otimes b$ over the open and zero elsewhere. It is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks]; [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] makes this a derived comparison. To justify the K-flat computation, termwise $j_!$ preserves flatness and K-flatness: $(j_!Q)\otimes L\cong j_!(Q\otimes j^*L)$ by the same stalk formula, $j^*$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and $j_!$ is exact. For the proper part define $S_YRr_{*,A}L\to Rr_{*,B}S_{\bar X}L$ as the $B$-adjoint of the map $r_B^*S_YRr_{*,A}L\cong S_{\bar X}r_A^*Rr_{*,A}L\to S_{\bar X}L$ obtained from the $A$-counit. Its restriction to $A$ is the projection map with coefficient $B$, followed by the inverse of $Rr_{*,A}\operatorname{Res}\cong\operatorname{Res}Rr_{*,B}$ from [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]. This is the same map, since taking its proper adjoint is precisely tensoring the proper counit with $B$. The unbounded ordinary proper projection formula [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] makes it invertible. Restriction of scalars reflects isomorphisms because the underlying cohomology sheaves are unchanged; no faithfulness assertion for derived morphisms is needed. Composing the proper and open maps defines the $B$-linear isomorphism $c_M$. Its definition is compatible with refinement and composition by [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] and adjunction pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. For consecutive quotients these proper adjoints are both the original counit tensored twice, identified by $(x\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto x\otimes bc$; the open maps have the identical formula. This proves the cocycle for $c$. Applying $C$, which preserves tensor, identifies this comparison with the pro-etale compactification comparison: at the proper part both are the adjoints of the same counit square by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], and at the open part both are the identity/zero map by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. The bounded-below site comparisons apply on the right since $S_XM$ is bounded; on the left the proper projection formula identifies the tensor expression with that bounded-below complex before making the comparison.

source.place: 2.13.1–2.13.2 and 3.1.12.1; the latter supplies restriction of scalars only, while the cited proper projection formula supplies derived extension of scalars.

proof.text:
Compare the actual normalized traces. In the ordinary categories one has the equality of $B$-linear morphisms
$$T^B_{S_YK}\circ P_B(\lambda_K)\circ c_{H_AK}=S_Y(T^A_K).\tag{*}$$
Use the common annihilator $N=\ell^r$ to construct both traces in [lem-pur-torsion-top-trace]. Independence of the annihilator in that statement identifies this construction for $B$ with the one using $\ell^m$ and the power-map twist in Step 4. Write $U=Rh_{!,A}A_X(d)[2d]$ with $h=f$, and $t=t_{f,\ell^r}:U\to A_Y$. That theorem specifies $T^A_K$ as the inverse projection formula followed by $1_K\otimes_A^Lt$; it specifies $T^B_{S_YK}$, still with the same annihilator, as the inverse projection formula followed by $1_{S_YK}\otimes_A^Lt$. On identifying both sources in (*) with $(S_YK)\otimes_A^LU$, the two arrows are exactly $1_{S_YK}\otimes_A^Lt$ to $S_YK$. The identification of the sources agrees with $P_B(\lambda_K)c_{H_AK}$: for the proper part the two projection maps have adjoints given by the same proper counit with tensor factors reassociated; for the open part both send $(q\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $q\otimes ab$. This uses the explicit projection map of [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] and the adjunction-pasting identity [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between projection-formula objects. In particular for $K=A_Y$ this identifies $t_B$ with $S_Yt_A$ via $c$ and the twist comparison. The calculation takes place in $D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ from its construction, so it does not infer equality of morphisms from forgetting the $B$-action. The site comparisons of Steps 3 and 5, being compatible with the same tensor maps and counits, give precisely the same equality of pro-etale traces.

source.place: 2.13.2 with one common annihilator; 1.1.1; comparison of the actual tensor-with-trace maps, not an application of restriction-of-scalars compatibility alone.

proof.text:
Take adjoints to obtain the exceptional coefficient map. Let $\epsilon_A:P_AG_A\to1$ be the ordinary counit. Define the canonical map
$$b_K:S_XG_AK\longrightarrow G_BS_YK$$
as the $B$-adjoint of
$$P_BS_XG_AK\xrightarrow{c_{G_AK}^{-1}}S_YP_AG_AK\xrightarrow{S_Y\epsilon_{A,K}}S_YK.$$
This is well typed: Step 2 identifies $G_AK$ with $H_AK$, so it is bounded finite Tor by Step 3 and Step 5 applies. Under the $B$-adjunction, the left side of
$$b_K\circ S_X\gamma^A_K=\gamma^B_{S_YK}\circ\lambda_K\tag{**}$$
corresponds to $S_Y(\epsilon_{A,K}\circ P_A\gamma^A_K)\circ c_{H_AK}^{-1}=S_YT^A_K\circ c_{H_AK}^{-1}$, by naturality of $c$ and the defining adjoint equation for $b$. The right side corresponds to $T^B_{S_YK}\circ P_B\lambda_K$. These agree by (*), and injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves (**). Both $\gamma$ maps are isomorphisms by Step 2, derived reduction preserves isomorphisms, and $\lambda$ is an isomorphism by Step 4. Therefore (**) also proves that $b_K$ is an isomorphism. This does not assert that the mate of an arbitrary invertible transformation is invertible. By [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], and the proper/open counit normalizations in Steps 3 and 5, $C_Xb_K$ is exactly the exceptional-image coefficient comparison for the explicitly defined transported functor. Thus (**) is the coefficient compatibility in the question, on its specified intrinsic categories. Setting $r=n+1,m=n$ gives the displayed adjacent-level assertion.

source.place: 3.2.3–3.2.5, taking the adjoint of 2.13.2; the additional coefficient comparison is constructed explicitly as the adjoint of scalar extension of the counit.

proof.text: Cocycle and the unit coefficient. For $r\geq m\geq n$ compose (**) for $r\to m$ and $m\to n$. Tensor associativity of Step 4 and its cocycle for $\lambda$ identify the result, after precomposing with $S_{r,n}\gamma^{A_r}_K$, with $\gamma^{A_n}_{S_{r,n}K}\lambda_{r,n,K}$, which is also the result for the direct $r\to n$ comparison. Cancel the isomorphism $S_{r,n}\gamma^{A_r}_K$; the two $b$ maps coincide. The identity quotient is the identity by its defining counit/adjoint formula. This proves the full quotient cocycle for the exceptional maps and for the compatible purity maps, not just pairwise existence. If $K=A_{n,Y}$, then $H_{A_n}K=A_{n,X}(d)[2d]$. Its twist is a finite locally free rank-one sheaf by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], so it is constructible and concentrated in degree zero before the shift, and hence in degree $-2d$ after the shift. Its derived quotient is the corresponding lower-level line by the power-map computation of Step 4, with the same cocycle. Steps 2–3 and (**) give exactly these assertions for $Rf_n^!A_{n,Y}$. For $d=0$ the new trace theorem identifies the trace with the etale sum counit, giving the required dimension-zero normalization. Empty sources give zero objects and the same formulas remain valid.

source.place: 1.1.1, 2.9 dimension-zero normalization, 2.13.2 and 3.2.5; elementary cancellation of the already established isomorphisms for three coefficient levels.

proof_origin.place: XVIII 2.9, 2.13.2, 3.2.3–3.2.5; ordinary affine-space/etale-local nondegeneracy and explicit derived scalar-extension mate calculation spelling out the quotient cocycle.
